newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST - China GDP seen growing 10.3 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - China GDP seen growing 10.3 pct in 1997.

text.p: China's gross domestic product (GDP) is seen growing by about 10 percent in 1996 and by 10.3 percent in 1997, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.

Inflation would drop to about seven percent in 1996, further falling to 6.7 percent in 1997, Xinhua quoted a report by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the State Statistical Bureau as saying.
China's GDP grew by 10.2 percent in 1995 and Beijing has set an official growth target of eight percent for 1996.
Inflation was 14.8 percent in 1995, with an official target of 10 percent set for this year.
Fixed asset investment would climb to 2.35 trillion yuan ($283 billion) in 1996, a rise in real terms of 10.7 percent compared to last year, the report said.
Fixed asset investment in 1997 would increase by 12.5 percent in real terms compared to this year, reaching a total of 2.80 trillion yuan, the report predicted.

China's fixed asset investment rose by 18.6 percent in the first six months of 1996 to 670.8 billion yuan, with the pace of growth falling 6.9 percentage points compared with the year-ago period, official figures show.
The report urged the government to keep a tight lid on fixed asset investment, warning that capital construction could careen out of control.
"With the lowering of interest rates twice this year, many localities felt a strong urge to launch new construction projects," Xinhua quoted the report as saying.
China should strive to make efficiency and quality the engine of economic growth rather than simply increasing output, it said.
"There still exist severe problems, such as wasteful allocation of resources, poor efficiency and management," it said.
